exposure: Fetal diagnosis of Asymmetric Ventriculomegaly, Interhemispheric Cyst, and Dysgenesis of the Corpus Callosum (AVID)
outcome: Neurodevelopmental outcomes (sit independently, mainstream school, expressive language, near-normal development without seizures)
Mortality (fetal demise, neonatal/early infant death, later death)
cohort: 41 maternal-infant dyads with a fetal diagnosis of Asymmetric Ventriculomegaly, Interhemispheric Cyst, and Dysgenesis of the Corpus Callosum (AVID) identified from a fetal imaging database.
finding: Among 41 maternal-fetal dyads with AVID, a majority of children survived to the 2-year follow-up, all developed hydrocephalus, and while many had seizures, a significant proportion showed expressive language, mainstream school attendance, and near-normal development.
mod_finding: A majority of patients (68%) were delivered via cesarean section because their head size precluded vaginal delivery.
gest_age: A slight majority of patients (55%) were born before 36 weeks of gestational age.
